title: Isospin violation and the isovector suppression factor for xenon at 250 keV: per-isotope amplitudes, the f_n/f_p scan and what it does to the high-energy/low-energy ratio
question: For general f_n/f_p (elastic and inelastic O1, and O4 with proton/neutron spin structure), what do WimPyDD's per-isotope shell-model responses give for the amplitude Z F_p + r N F_n and its nodes, R_hi/lo(r), the xenophobic point at 248 keV, enriched/depleted targets and N_lo, and where does this agree or disagree with P032?
headline_result: Per-isotope shell-model amplitudes show xenon's second neutron-form-factor zeros span 231-259 keV, so the 248 keV rate is proton-dominated for every f_n/f_p (rho(248) = 0.93-1.20 over r in [-2,2]) while the low-energy rate varies x2500; P032's N_lo minimum 7.2 at r = -0.744 is confirmed independently (all common numbers within 0.5%, nodes within 0.4 keV); isospin violation buys shape, never absolute high-energy rate below delta = 380 keV; isotope engineering is not a decisive test
key_numbers: second zeros: F_p 279-302, F_n 231-259, isovector 173-190 (nat 182.2), isoscalar 251-278 (268.8) keV; node crosses 248 keV at r=-0.826; Helm 94.6/279.5; N_lo(1 TeV) 2743/1240/16.97/7.25/475/8412 at r=+1/0/-0.7/-0.744/-1/-2, <=10 only for r in [-0.76,-0.73], never <=5; r=-0.7: rho_lo 1.09e-3, rho_hi 0.176, rho_248 0.957, shape gain <=x378; delta=300/350 percentile of 248 keV 99.5/97.8 (iso), 70.7/51.0% (vec); delta=380 rho_hi <=3.4 annual (19 Sun-frame); 90% 136Xe: rate(248) x0.023 iso, x1.63 vec, 3sigma two-target test 124-1884 events; O4 S_p/S_n 0.029/0.026, iso/vec shapes within 5.7%, N_lo 28 -> 3.6 at c_n/c_p=-0.025 (rate x0.0021); validation 9e-15
model_or_mechanism: NREFT O1 and O4 with isospin-violating couplings c_n/c_p; WimPyDD DMFormFactor-v6 one-body M and Sigma'/Sigma'' responses; per-isotope kernel factorisation dR/dE = (1000/m) sum_i K_i eta(v_min,i)
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - no isospin structure rescues elastic SI; 248 keV is insensitive to f_n/f_p
confidence: medium - exact within WimPyDD one-body responses (validated 1e-14), node positions carry +-10 keV nuclear-structure uncertainty
